reasoning:
I verified the design's code claims first (all 10 anchors are unique by python str.count; buildToward does return a boolean; DOCT_SET really carries no spg/mlrs/sniper/radarv; `read >= 0.55` really is an existing idiom at ai.js:4797; Regular is read 0.35 so the gate does hold; behaviour check [29] reads only intel().arms/.mix so adding `learn:` will not move it; seenB records really do carry x/y so learnRazed's distance test is well-formed; WEAPONS ranges really are in tiles). The mechanical parts are careful and mostly correct.

The learning loop is not. I implemented the update rule exactly as written (n seeded 1, q seeded 0, first push sets the baseline and updates nothing, A = r - base with base a running mean at step 1/min(n,6), credit = cost share with the chosen arm floored at 0.34 and renormalised, q += (s/min(n,8))(A-q), score = (1-lam)p + lam*q + C*sqrt(ln(1+T)/n), lam = 0.75n/(n+2)) and ran it over 200 seeds at every tier.

Noiseless, the best possible case for a learner: all three q converge to exactly 0.000, spread exactly 0.000, and the truly WORST arm is chosen on 100% of decisions at Veteran, Elite, Commander and Warlord. With sigma=0.35 noise the spread is 0.07-0.11 against a true spread of 0.55, and the worst arm is still chosen 92-99% of the time; the third arm was chosen 0 times in 3,600 decisions. Worse still, sweeping the true gap 0.5 -> 1.0 -> 2.0 -> 3.0 shrinks the measured spread 0.081 -> 0.046 -> 0.005 -> 0.000 and tightens the lock-in 95.9% -> 100%: the loop performs worse the more there is to learn.

The mechanism is a self-referential baseline. `base` is ONE global running mean over the last <=6 pushes. The policy commits (the design boasts of this), so within that window every r came from the same posture, so base -> c + mu(incumbent), so A_incumbent -> 0 exactly, so q_incumbent -> 0, while the unpulled arms keep their seeded q = 0. All three estimates equal zero and the argmax reduces to (1-lam)p + bonus, a deterministic function of the priors and the pull counts that contains no outcome information at all. That is known fatal 1 reproduced exactly - q identical, spread 0.000, locked on ARMS[0] by prior - reached without any clamp. The design's own Step 1 assumes a mixing frequency f=(0.5,0.2,0.2,0.1) that its own policy provably does not produce; Steps 2-4 inherit the error, and the "worked opening" treats A as a persistent absolute when its own rule makes base chase r.

Three further defects compound it: MIN_CRED hands 34% of every push to a posture chosen AFTER that wave's hulls were bought (ai.js:3754 build block runs before the ai.js:4226 launch/settle block in the same think) - a one-push lag that is known fatal "attribution" with the sign flipped; the shared-A update applies one advantage to all three arms weighted by a stale, near-constant cost share, attenuating every gap by the share contrast (~0.1, exactly 0 when the composition is stationary, which `if (army.length < wantSize)` guarantees while a wave is winning); and the +2.0 clamp plus a repeatable razing credit (seenB `gone` is a flip-flop that noteSighting resets at ai.js:1145) poison the numerator. The kill radius is arm-scaled (12 tiles for armour vs 28.6 for a PzH-2000 gunline, a 5.7x catchment AREA), which rigs the very comparison it was written to un-rig.

I also validated the corrections: causal credit + centring at SCORE time instead of update time + a forced round-robin opening recovers a measured spread of 0.43-0.55 against a true 0.55 and drops the bad arm from 96% to 47-64%.

Finally, the acceptance suite would bless the dead build: measurement 8 asserts "the mean advantage A must sit near zero, which is the direct test that the centring is working" - and A is EXACTLY zero in the fully degenerate case. That is the same blindness as the old plan's "q STAYS INSIDE p +- 0.45 - PASS". Only measurement 3 would catch it, and its stated remedy (cut to two arms) does not touch the cause.

Verdict BROKEN: it repeats known fatal 1 and the attribution major, and adds three new ones.

fatals.which: DEGENERACY (repeat of known fatal 1): the baseline is captured by the incumbent, so every arm's estimate converges to exactly zero and the choice reduces to argmax of the doctrine prior
fatals.problem: `base` is ONE global running mean over the last <=6 pushes (step 1/min(baseN,6), BASE_N=6). The policy commits after one or two pushes - the design boasts of this in 'DOES IT ACTUALLY EXPLOIT?' - so within the baseline's own window every r came from the SAME posture. Therefore base -> c + mu(incumbent), not c + mu-bar. Then A_incumbent = r - base -> 0 EXACTLY, so q_incumbent -> 0; the unpulled arms keep their seeded q = 0. All three estimates are zero, the lam*q term cancels out of every pairwise comparison, and score(a) collapses to (1-lam_a)*p_a + C*sqrt(ln(1+T)/n_a) - a deterministic function of the priors and the pull counts with no outcome information in it at all. Worked exactly, noiseless, Elite (read 0.80, C=0.096), NATO-style priors p=(+0.30,-0.07,-0.30): push 1 score=(0.338,0.061,-0.112) -> armour; push 1 sets base and updates nothing; push 2 onward r is unchanged so A=0 every push and q stays (0,0,0) for ever; at push 11 score_armour = 0.365*0.30 + 0.635*0 + 0.096*sqrt(ln14/11) = 0.157 against gunline 0.103 and swarm -0.069. Result: pulls 11/1/1, q = (0.000,0.000,0.000), spread 0.000 - byte-for-byte the reviewer's measurement of the OLD block. For gunline ever to be tried you need 0.096*sqrt(ln(1+T)) > 0.162, i.e. T > 50 settled pushes; Elite yields 8-11. I simulated the rule verbatim over 200 seeds x 4 tiers: noiseless, spread 0.0000 and the truly WORST arm chosen on 100% of decisions at Veteran/Elite/Commander/Warlord, third arm chosen 0 times in 3,600 decisions. With sigma=0.35, spread 0.07-0.11 against a true spread of 0.55, worst arm 92-99%. And the decisive tell: sweeping the true gap 0.5/1.0/2.0/3.0 SHRINKS the measured spread 0.081/0.046/0.005/0.000 and TIGHTENS the lock 95.9%/98.5%/100%/100%. The loop gets worse the more there is to learn, because a bigger true gap makes the incumbent commit harder, which makes base its own mean more completely. The degeneracy_argument's Step 1 assumes f=(0.5,0.2,0.2,0.1) - five or six exploratory pulls out of eleven - which its own policy provably does not produce (measured 0.95/0.04/0.00); Steps 2-4 inherit that error, and the 'WORKED OPENING' with A=-0.40 on two consecutive pushes is impossible under its own rule because base chases r. Note also that the prior is NOT scaled by grip while C IS, so the lock is tightest at Veteran - the tier with the fewest pushes.
fatals.correction: Delete `base`, `baseN`, `BASE_N` and stop centring at UPDATE time. Centre at SCORE time instead, where no arm can capture its own yardstick: keep q_a as a plain running mean of the RAW ratio credited to a (`b.q += (s/Math.min(b.n,NCAP)) * (r - b.q)`), and in chooseArm score `(1-lam)*b.p + lam*(b.q - qbar) + C*sqrt(...)` with qbar = the n-weighted mean of the ready arms' q. Every battle-common term c cancels in that subtraction exactly as the design wants, but the reference is the OTHER arms' estimates rather than the recent reward stream, so an exploited arm cannot drive its own advantage to zero. Additionally force exploration rather than bonusing it: while any ready arm has n < 2, pick the least-pulled ready arm outright. With C=0.096 and pairwise prior gaps up to 0.60, sqrt(ln(1+T)/n) cannot sample the other arms inside 8-14 pushes. I ran these two fixes plus fix 2 below: measured spread rises to 0.43-0.55 against a true 0.55 and the bad arm falls from 96% to 47-64%.

fatals.which: ATTRIBUTION (repeat of the known attribution major, sign-flipped): MIN_CRED gives 34% of every push to the posture chosen AFTER that wave was built
fatals.problem: The ARMY COMPOSITION block (js/ai.js:3754, where `_arm` is stamped and buildToward spends) and the ATTACK WAVES block (js/ai.js:4226, where the edit puts `if (ep) learnSettle();`) are in the SAME think(), build first. learnSettle ends with chooseArm(), then launchGroundWave -> bookWave -> learnCommit sets `ep.arm = armNow` and reads `u._arm`. So the posture chosen at settle k has literally zero causal influence on the wave launched microseconds later - those hulls were bought under the previous posture and carry its tag. The new posture influences production during that wave's life, which becomes wave k+1. The design names this the fix for the attribution major ('credit is read off what the wave was MADE OF') and then bolts `w[e.arm] = Math.max(w[e.arm], e.cost*MIN_CRED)` on top, which is exactly 'the arm chosen at settle k built wave k' off by one in the other direction. It is not a harmless belt-and-braces: because the legacy shares are near-constant (see next fatal), the 0.34 floor is the ONLY source of contrast between the credit vectors, so the loop's entire nominal signal is carried by the one third that is misattributed. And where two arms' legacy shares already exceed 0.34 - e.g. (0.40,0.35,0.25) - choosing armour and choosing gunline produce LITERALLY IDENTICAL weight vectors, so the credit carries no information about the choice at all.
fatals.correction: Delete MIN_CRED and stop crediting `ep.arm`. Keep an `armPrev` (the posture in force during the production window that actually bought this wave) and use it as the untagged fallback in learnCommit instead of armNow. Then move chooseArm() out of learnSettle so the choice governs the window it will be scored on: call it immediately after learnCommit (or at the top of think, before the ai.js:3754 build block), and score each episode against the arm that was in force while its hulls were bought.

fatals.which: NEW: one advantage is applied to all three arms weighted by a stale, near-constant cost share, which attenuates every gap toward zero and is exactly zero in the stationary case
fatals.problem: `b.q += (s_a / Math.min(b.n, NCAP)) * (A - b.q)` runs for EVERY arm with s_a > 0, with the SAME A. So q_a is not an estimate of arm a at all - it is a differently-smoothed copy of one reward stream. Its fixed point is q_a = E[s_a*A]/E[s_a] = E[A] + cov(s_a,A)/E[s_a], and with symmetric shares that equals (h - l)*(mu_a - mu-bar), where h - l is the share contrast between 'a was chosen' and 'a was not'. Surviving hulls keep `u._arm` for ever and `if (army.length < wantSize)` (js/ai.js:3757) stops ALL production while the wave is at strength - the design says so itself - so the share vector barely moves between pushes and h - l is carried only by the 0.34 floor: h - l ~= 0.10, i.e. the estimated gap is a TENTH of the true gap, far below the design's own stated per-push noise of sigma ~= 0.35. In the exact stationary limit (light attrition, or legacy shares where the floor never bites) h = l and the three q's are three smoothings of the same number: spread exactly 0. The degeneracy_argument's Step 3 - 'E[q1] - E[q2] = mu(1) - mu(2), Exactly, with no scaling constant and no residual bias' - is algebraically false; it silently treats the credit as if each push went to ONE arm. Compare the residual signal to the prior term it must beat: (1-lam)*Delta_p is at minimum 0.25*0.60 = 0.15, while lam*Delta_q is at most 0.75*0.05 = 0.0375, and even the UCB bonus difference (0.091 at T=12) is larger than the learned signal. Related quantitative error: armPrior clamps each p to +-0.30 SEPARATELY, so the pairwise gap is up to 0.60, not the 0.30 the design asserts. Every downstream number is off by 2x - at lam=0.5625 (n=6) you need Delta_q > 0.467 to overturn a maximal prior, against a measured Delta_q of 0.07.
fatals.correction: Credit the push to the causal arm only, or share only over NEW purchases. Either (a) `b.n += 1; b.q += (1/min(b.n,NCAP))*(r - b.q)` for the single arm in force during the production window; or (b) if shares are kept, accumulate `ep.share` over hulls bought SINCE THE LAST SETTLE (stamp `u._born = epN` the first time a unit is seen in groundArmy and share over those only) rather than over the whole standing army. Either restores a contrast near 1.0. Also correct the prior arithmetic: state the pairwise bound as 0.60 and re-derive the 'observed 0.10 overturns it' claim, or clamp the SPREAD across arms rather than each arm.

fatals.which: NEW: the +2.0 clamp is a value clamp that binds at the top, and the razing credit is unbounded and repeatable because seenB `gone` is a flip-flop
fatals.problem: Two halves, both in the numerator. (a) `r = U.clamp((kills + razed - lost)/cost, -1.2, 2.0)` is a clamp on a VALUE - the exact machine the design says it removed - and it binds at the top end: WORTH gives conyard 2400, refinery 2600, factory 1500, lpar_* 2400 (js/ai.js:397-414), so a wave that gets inside a base books 5,000-8,000 of razings against a 4,700-credit 1950s KPA wave and saturates at 2.0. Two different successful pushes become one value, on precisely the pushes that carry the most information. The bottom clamp at -1.2 is unreachable (lost <= cost makes r >= -1) so all the protection is at the wrong end. (b) `learnRazed` is hooked at the `r.gone = true` transition in forgetStale, but `gone` is NOT terminal: noteSighting resets `rec.gone = false; rec.t = now` whenever the structure is seen again (js/ai.js:1145). So a still-standing enemy building that drifts in and out of contact books its full worth again on every cycle, without limit. And forgetStale's test is `staleness(r.tx, r.ty, now) < 6 && r.t < now - 6` where r.tx/r.ty is the building's TOP-LEFT tile while noteContact measures to its CENTRE (js/ai.js:1128) - for a 4x4 conyard the look grid can cover (tx,ty) from ~2.8 tiles outside sighting range, so an intact 2,400-credit conyard books as razed, returns on the next sighting, and books again. This is a reward-farming channel, it is unbounded, and it favours the posture that loiters at standoff range.
fatals.correction: Clamp the STEP, never the value: remove the +2.0 ceiling and instead cap the razing contribution per push (e.g. `ep.razed = Math.min(ep.razed, ep.cost)`), or bound the per-push movement of q rather than r. Make the razing credit one-way and once per structure: `if (!r.razedOnce) { r.razedOnce = 1; learnRazed(r); }` and set that flag where the record is DELETED (the second forgetStale hit, `if (r.gone) seenB.delete(id)`), which is the only transition noteSighting cannot undo. Also fix the tile mismatch by testing staleness at the building's centre tile rather than at r.tx/r.ty.

fatals.which: NEW: the kill/raze radius is scaled by the posture's own weapon reach, which rigs the comparison it was written to un-rig
fatals.problem: `ep.r = Math.max(12, reach + 4) * CFG.TILE` off the wave's own deepest ground weapon. Armour's MBT gun gives 12 tiles; a gunline wave with pzh2000_l52 (range 24.6, js/rules.js:1788) gives 28.6, koksan (20.0, js/rules.js:2273) gives 24.0, mlrs (14.0, js/rules.js:43) gives 18.0. That is a 5.7x catchment AREA for gunline - a 28.6-tile disc is ~2,570 tiles, about 12% of the 144-tile theatre - inside which every hostile death and every struck-off structure is credited regardless of who caused it. The fog_argument concedes 'proximity is not causation' and then claims 'it is identical for all three postures so it cannot bias the ranking between them'. It is not identical: it is a direct function of the posture's own weapon mix, so the foreign-credit bias is perfectly correlated with the arm being scored. Measurement 5's 15% tolerance is derived for one radius and silently applied to three; at 5.7x the area the gunline arm would blow through it while armour sat inside it, and the loop would read that difference as gunline being better. Secondary: `ep.kills += r.cost || 300` prices enemy hulls at the catalogue `e.def.cost` while `ep.lost += P.factionCost(u.def)` and `ep.cost` price ours at our own multiplier, so the ratio's two halves are on different scales (constant within a match, so it cancels in a correct advantage, but it is not the like-for-like exchange the text claims).
fatals.correction: Use ONE radius for every posture. Either a fixed generous constant (16 tiles) about the wave centroid, or - better, and reach-independent - credit a kill by distance to the NEAREST LIVE WAVE MEMBER rather than to the centroid, with a small fixed halo (4-6 tiles). That gives the gunline wave its long fight geometry without handing it a 5.7x catchment, because a dispersed battery covers more ground only where it actually has vehicles. Price kills with the same function used for our own losses so the exchange is genuinely like-for-like. Finally, note that the acceptance suite as written would bless the degenerate build: measurement 8's 'the mean advantage A must sit near zero, which is the direct test that the centring is working' is EXACTLY satisfied when the loop is dead (A = 0 identically), which is the same blindness as the old plan's 'q STAYS INSIDE p +- 0.45 - PASS'. Replace it with a test that cannot pass on a dead loop: assert max(q) - min(q) > 0 AND that the pull counts change in response to reward, and keep measurement 3 as the gate.

reasoning:
I read js/ai.js (5,768 lines) and every function the design names: intelSweep (987), noteContact (1119), noteSighting (1132), forgetStale (1245), staleness (1287), liveTrack (1307), trackedEntity (1309), reapWave (1439), counterMix (1821), buildToward (2026), doctrine (350), worthOf (416), groundArmy (4944), bookWave (5103), launchGroundWave (4729), init (618-698), intel() (5703), plus _behtest.html, player.js and rules.js.

WHAT CHECKS OUT, first, because it matters for the verdict: all ten anchors count exactly 1 under python str.count, including the long edit-9 block ("const army = groundArmy();" alone appears twice, at 3259 and 3754, but the anchor's comment prefix disambiguates it). buildToward really does return a boolean (`return true` / `return false` on every path), so the `bought` chain is well-formed. DIFF.regular carries read 0.35 and no PERSONALITY entry overrides `read`, and _behtest.html line 37 does default opt-diff to "regular" while the harness at 333-337 never sets it — so learnOn() is false throughout the suite, stanceMix returns counterMix's own object, stanceSplit returns -1, the release branch cannot fire (neither of its guards matches hold === -1), and the two buildToward calls run in the same order with the same arguments. DOCT_SET (js/ai.js:224) genuinely carries no spg/mlrs/sniper/radarv, and dm.heavy.mbt / heavy.heavy / heavy.at / infantry.mg / infantry.rifle all exist. No new G.rng() call. The gate claim and the byte-identity claim are, as far as I can tell statically, honest.

THE FOG ARGUMENT, attacked specifically. I could not find an input that reads enemy units[], buildings[], cash, tech, queues, production or era. counterMix's input is foeArms() over seenU aged at D.memory, which is already the fogged reading. doctrine() takes no picture. worthOf() reads WORTH and BUILDINGS, static. There is no field read that is populated only for the human player: `dead`, `lastHitBy`, `def.cost`, `def.cat` are all universal on entities, and seenB has carried `cost: e.def.cost || 300` since the picture was written, so `cost` on seenU is the same class of fact. The fog argument is substantially sound and I am saying so.

But it is not sound where it matters. The design's own defence of its one admitted bound is: "it is identical for all three postures so it cannot bias the ranking between them." That sentence is false of the code the same document specifies. learnCommit sets ep.r = max(12, deepest ground weapon + 4) tiles, explicitly so that gunline is not "measured on a shorter ruler". An armour wave's deepest ground weapon is the tank gun at 8.0 tiles or the tank destroyer at 9.6 (counterMix's own comments), giving ep.r = 13.6; a gunline wave carries the MLRS at 23.2, giving ep.r = 27.2. That is 4.0x the area — 2,320 tiles, eleven per cent of a 144x144 theatre, nearly all of it in fog. Every kill and every razing inside that disc that our push did not cause is credited to whichever posture fields the longest tube. The unearned-credit rate is therefore a direct function of the arm, and it is largest for exactly the arm the doctrine prior refuses to speak for. Measurement 5 asks for the aggregate misattribution share but never breaks it down by posture, so the design's own probe cannot see it. That is a new fatal, and it is a fog fatal: the reward pays a posture for owning an MLRS rather than for what the MLRS killed.

And three more, of which the first is decisive.

Two smaller accuracy defects in the fog section, for the record: (1) "I touch r.ref.dead inside that window and nowhere else" is false of learnKills' own first line, `if (r.scored || !r.ref || !r.ref.dead) continue;`, which dereferences ref on every seenU record — up to D.memory = 600s old at Commander — before liveTrack is tested. No information reaches a decision, so it is not a leak, but the file's invariant is about touching ref at all and the claim of compliance is wrong. (2) "seenU, which is written ONLY by noteContact -> noteSighting" is false: intelSweep's esmSweep block (js/ai.js:1063-1085) calls noteSighting(e, now) directly for any emitting radar or jammer within 1.9x its own emitter range, bypassing noteContact's sub, stealth and buildProgress gates. Those records carry a live ref and are eligible for kill credit at a range no sensor of ours ever saw them from. It is still an honest ESM fix, so not a leak either — but the enumeration of "four gates before a credit" does not describe every record learnKills walks.

Non-fatal corrections worth folding in: armReady tests mbt for armour, spg for gunline, rifle+at for swarm — and the design's own critique of the previous attempt is that "the old armReady tested spg and mbt, which every faction owns in every era, so it reduced to P.tech >= 2 and prevented nothing." All eight rosters carry an spg (spg_n/p/c/k/r/g/b/f in rules.js) and an mbt; rifle and at are universal. ready is 1 below tech 2 and 3 at or above it: the new gate is P.tech >= 2 verbatim, and the owner's realism promise is never exercised. Separately, the prior gap arithmetic is 2x optimistic: p = clamp((raw-mean)*0.6, ±0.30) over three arms gives a maximum gap of 0.60, not 0.30, so the "an observed advantage gap of 0.10 overturns it" figure should read 0.20. Kills are priced at raw def.cost while losses are priced at P.factionCost, and FACTIONS costMul runs 0.68 (KPA) to 1.45 (ROC), so a KPA commander over-reports every exchange ratio by ~47% and a ROC one under-reports; common-mode within a match, but it moves where the (-1.2, +2.0) clamp bites. The split release fires whenever the preferred queue merely has queueLen >= 2 rather than only when it bought nothing, so the hold leaks continuously. And `if (!u._arm) u._arm = armNow` runs over the whole of groundArmy(), not over new production, so on the first learn-enabled think the opening posture inherits the tag — and the credit — for the entire army bought before any posture existed.

Verdict: BROKEN. Fatal 1 reproduces the outcome of known fatal 1 (one arm for the whole match, the loop a no-op) by a new mechanism, and fatals 2-4 are new.

fatals.which: The centred reward + UCB policy (learnSettle's baseline, chooseArm, and the whole of degeneracy_argument)
fatals.problem: The design contains a contradiction it proves on itself. degeneracy_argument Step 1 needs base -> c + SUM_a f_a mu(a) with the pull frequencies f_a mixed; the 'DOES IT ACTUALLY EXPLOIT?' section then proves the policy commits, i.e. f collapses onto one arm. Both cannot hold. base is a running mean of OUR OWN pushes with step 1/min(n,6), so once the incumbent is being played every push, base converges on the incumbent's own mean and A_incumbent = r - base has expectation EXACTLY ZERO no matter how bad that posture is. q_incumbent -> 0 by construction. The estimator therefore measures changes, never levels: a uniformly failing posture reads A ~ 0 and is never abandoned on evidence. What is left of the incumbent's score is (1-lam)*p + C*sqrt(ln(1+T)/n), which contains no information about the battle at all, so the switch to a second posture happens on a timer fixed by (p, C, lam) alone. Worked on the design's own constants with q pinned at 0 and a prior gap of 0.30: Veteran (C=0.072) never tries a second posture in 15 pushes against a 6-8 push horizon; Elite (C=0.096) first tries one at push 13 against an 8-11 push horizon; Commander at push 9 of 11-14. Even with a modest 0.165 gap Elite reaches push 7. So on the two tiers the loop is gated to and actually reaches, the commander picks argmax(doctrine) at push 1 and never revisits it - which is fatal 1's measured outcome (one arm forever, 20 waves to arrive back at today's behaviour) restored by a different route, and it makes 'three arms get two to six pulls each' false: arms 2 and 3 get zero or one. The design's own WORKED OPENING is likewise impossible under its own rule: it feeds A = -0.40 on two consecutive armour pushes, but base was set from armour's first push, so the second armour push scores A = r2 - r1 ~ 0, not -0.40.
fatals.correction: Two changes, both required. (a) Force round-robin initialisation: pushes 1..3 play armour, gunline, swarm in a fixed order regardless of score, and only the pushes after that go through chooseArm. UCB1's guarantee assumes each arm is pulled once before the index is trusted, and at a 6-14 push horizon this is the only thing that makes the comparison exist at all. Set the baseline from push 1 as now, but do not update q until push 3 has settled, so the first advantage is measured against a baseline that contains all three arms. (b) Stop the baseline chasing the incumbent: replace `base += (r-base)/min(++baseN,6)` with a true cumulative mean over all settled pushes (`base += (r-base)/(++baseN)`, no floor), which at this horizon is the arm-mixture mean rather than a 6-push tracker, and additionally hold a per-arm last-reward so the advantage of the incumbent is computed against the mean of the OTHER arms' most recent rewards rather than against a number it wrote itself. If after (a) and (b) the switch still lands past push 8 at Elite, cut to two arms (armour, swarm) as measurement 3 already contemplates, rather than raising EXPLORE.

fatals.which: learnCommit's per-push credit radius, ep.r = max(12, deepest ground weapon + 4) tiles, and the fog_argument's 'THE ONE RESIDUAL LIMIT' paragraph
fatals.problem: fog_argument defends the proximity bound with 'it is identical for all three postures so it cannot bias the ranking between them.' The code makes it posture-dependent on purpose. An armour wave's deepest ground weapon is the tank gun at 8.0 tiles or the tank destroyer at 9.6 (counterMix's own comments), so ep.r = 13.6 tiles; a gunline wave carries the SPG at 20.4 and the MLRS at 23.2, so ep.r = 27.2 tiles. That is 4.0x the area - about 2,320 tiles, eleven per cent of a 144x144 theatre, almost all of it fog. Both ep.kills and ep.razed are gated on that same disc, so gunline harvests four times the area of kills it did not cause and razings it did not perform: the human's artillery duel 25 tiles away, a third party's base being flattened, an enemy column dying to its own minefield. The reward therefore pays a posture for FIELDING a long-ranged tube rather than for what the tube killed, and it pays it most to the one arm doctrine() has no prior for and that must 'earn its place from evidence'. Measurement 5 asks only for the aggregate misattribution share and never splits it by posture, so the design's own probe is blind to the exact bias the design claims cannot exist.
fatals.correction: Attribute rather than approximate. `e.lastHitBy = shooter || null` is set on every entity in combat.js:955 and digest() already reads it on our own units, so inside the liveTrack window - where the design is already allowed to touch ref - test `r.ref.lastHitBy && r.ref.lastHitBy.owner === P` instead of a distance. That is strictly more honest than proximity, removes the residual bound the design says it cannot close, and removes the radius argument entirely. If that is rejected, then ep.r must be ONE constant for all three postures (12 tiles, the current floor) and gunline's reach must be compensated elsewhere - and measurement 5 must report the not-killed-by-us share broken down per posture, since a single aggregate number cannot falsify the claim being made.

fatals.which: learnKills gate (c) and learnRazed's hook in forgetStale - both of which depend on staleness()
fatals.problem: The look grid is `look = new Uint8Array(G.map.W * G.map.H)` (js/ai.js:628) and intelSweep stamps `Math.max(1, Math.min(255, (now/4)|0))` (js/ai.js:995). The stamp saturates at 255, i.e. game time 1020 s. staleness() returns `now - b*4`, so from t = 1026 s (17:06) every tile on the map reads staleness > 6 for ever. Two consequences, both fatal to the reward. learnKills' gate `staleness(...) <= 6` rejects 100 per cent of kills from that moment. And forgetStale's own `staleness(r.tx, r.ty, now) < 6` never holds again, so no structure is ever struck off the plot - which means learnRazed, the entire fix for known fatal 2, never fires again either. From 17 minutes onward every push scores r = -lost/cost, in [-1.2, 0]: both positive terms are structurally zero and the book learns only which posture loses least. The design specifies 25-minute matches and measures 'the learner's mean reward over the last third of the match' (measurements 3 and 4) - that window is entirely inside the dead zone. Measurement 8's 'razed must be non-zero on at least one push per match' passes vacuously on the early pushes and cannot detect it. The baseline makes it worse rather than absorbing it: base tracks with step 1/6, so the two or three pushes spanning the cliff take a large negative advantage that is charged to whichever posture happened to be in force at 17 minutes.
fatals.correction: Widen the grid: `look = new Uint16Array(G.map.W * G.map.H)` with `stamp = Math.max(1, Math.min(65535, (now/4)|0))`, which costs 20 kB more per commander (the file already argues 20 kB is nothing) and buys 72 hours. That one edit is needed anyway - forgetStale, pruneHypotheses and the ore-site scan at 3681/3693 are all silently broken past 17 minutes today - so it is a prerequisite edit, not an optional one, and it must be listed as an eleventh anchored edit rather than assumed. Additionally drop learnKills' gate (c) outright: liveTrack already guarantees the contact was held within 5 s, which necessarily means the tile was overlooked within 5 s, so the staleness test adds nothing to the kill credit and only couples it to a saturating counter.

fatals.which: The reapWave loss hook combined with learnWatch's settle condition
fatals.problem: ep.lost is accumulated in reapWave(), which runs on think()'s clock (D.think = 2.8 s at Regular, 2.1 at Veteran, 1.6 at Elite, 0.9 at Warlord). learnSettle() is fired from learnWatch(), which runs on intelSweep's 0.8 s clock, the moment `attackWave` contains no living member. A unit killed between two thinks is still in attackWave with u.dead set and its cost unbooked; learnWatch sees n = 0, settles, and ep - with those casualties missing - is discarded. The design deliberately sweeps kills BEFORE declaring the wave over ('the final exchange of an annihilated wave is its most expensive one') but leaves the matching losses on the slower clock, so an annihilated wave keeps all of its final kills and loses up to a full think-window of its own dead. A 16-unit, 8,000-credit wave that collapses in its last exchange can report lost = 5,500, scoring r = -0.69 where the truth is -1.00. The bias is upward on precisely the worst pushes, it is not common-mode (a posture that gets wiped out more often collects more of it, and the fastest-collapsing posture collects the most), and it is the identical asymmetry the design says it removed by abandoning `graves` - 'graves under-count exactly the pushes that went worst, which is the direction of bias that most corrupts a ranking.'
fatals.correction: Book the casualty once, at the point of death, and make the settle drain the wave first. In reapWave use a dedicated flag so the accounting cannot double-count: `if (ep && u._ep === epN && !u._lost) { u._lost = 1; ep.lost += P.factionCost(u.def); }`. Then in learnWatch, immediately before the `if (!n || now - ep.t > ...) learnSettle();` line, sweep the wave for stragglers on the picture's own clock: `for (const u of attackWave) if (u.dead && ep && u._ep === epN && !u._lost) { u._lost = 1; ep.lost += P.factionCost(u.def); }`. That puts losses on the same 0.8 s clock the kill sweep already runs on, which is the design's own stated reason for not leaving the kill sweep on think().

reasoning:
VERIFIED CLAIMS (the design is honest about these):

- Anchors: all 10 appear exactly once. `python3 str.count` on /Users/hjiang/Desktop/redalert/js/ai.js returns 1 for every one, including the 24-line anchor 9. No anchor is ambiguous.
- Test [29] is NOT broken. _behtest.html:333-337 sets only opt-map/era/aera/cash/seed/fog/3d; opt-diff keeps its `selected` default of "regular" (line 37) = DIFF.regular.read 0.35 < LEARN_READ 0.55. No PERSONALITY entry mods `read` (ai.js PERSONALITY table carries only waveTime/waveSize/aggro/defenceBias/techBias/earlyRush/airBias/navalBias/artyBias/econBias). intel() line 5711 still calls the unedited counterMix for `mix`, and [29] stringifies only `.mix`, so the four printed figures and the JSON compare are untouched. At hold=-1 the rewritten wave block reduces to the two original buildToward calls in the original order with the original arguments, and the release branch cannot fire. bookInit()'s early doctrine() call is pure and cache-keyed, consumes no G.rng(). Byte-identity holds.
- The four known fatals are NOT literally repeated. (1) No clamp on q anywhere; the reward is centred. (2) Razings are credited at forgetStale's `gone` transition and that line is reachable (staleness<6 && r.t<now-6 is satisfied by a wave standing in the enemy base). (3) All three postures are constructible: swarm needs tech 0 + rifle + at; armour tech 2 + mbt; gunline tech 2 + spg — and a posture is applied directly to counterMix's output and to the queue gate, so nothing downstream can refuse it. (4) The window really is liveTrack: ai.js:1307 is `G.time - r.t <= 5`, and noteContact:1120 `if (!e || e.dead || e.carried) return;` freezes r.t at the last live sighting, so the 5s gate is sound. seenU records survive death (forgetStale only deletes at `now - r.t > max(tau*2.5, D.memory)` ≥ 65s), so the sweep can actually see `r.ref.dead`.

WHERE IT BREAKS. The design does not repeat the old fatals — it reaches the old SYMPTOM by a new route, and it breaks its own central mechanism.

The decisive one is the baseline. `base` is a running mean of r over the pushes the policy actually took. The policy is designed to commit ("0.172 > 0.046: the leader is not unseated"). Those two properties are incompatible: once the incumbent is being pulled every push, base converges on the incumbent's own mean, so A = r - base collapses to noise, q_incumbent decays to 0, and the two unpulled arms sit at their seeded q = 0. All three learned values are ~0 and score(a) = (1-λ)·p + bonus — the doctrine prior decides, permanently. The design's own worked spread (q = +0.12/-0.03/-0.13/-0.28) is computed at f = (0.5,0.2,0.2,0.1) over 20 waves; at the horizon it actually claims (Veteran 6-8 settled pushes, minus one for the yardstick) with a committing policy the realistic pull vector is (5,1,0). base has step 1/min(baseN,6), so it catches up by push 3-4. Two informative pushes per match, then the signal is cancelled by construction. That is the old outcome — argmax returns a fixed arm for the whole battle — with the clamp swapped for a self-cancelling yardstick.

The prior arithmetic compounds it and is simply wrong. p = clamp((raw-mean)*0.6, ±0.30), so the maximum GAP between two priors is 0.60, not the 0.30 the design states. The claim "at λ=0.75 an observed advantage gap of 0.10 overturns it" therefore needs 0.20, and λ=0.75 is the n→∞ limit; at the realistic n=4 λ=0.5 and the required learned gap is the full 0.60, at n=2 it is 1.00. Worked forward with p=(+0.30,-0.15,-0.15) and a catastrophic A=-0.5 every push, the incumbent is not abandoned until push 5 — past the end of a Veteran match. With the baseline collapse it is never abandoned at all.

Then the integration. stanceSplit is called "the one lever that can change the SHAPE of the army" and measurement 2(a) rests on it, but its release condition is `!bought`, and buildToward (ai.js:2026-2059) returns false on `sum <= 0`, on queue saturation being handled by the caller's `queueLen < 2` gate never being entered, and on `P.cash < P.factionCost(def)*0.6` ("affordable roles exist; we are simply broke"). Saturation and scarcity are the two most common states of that block, and under scarcity the gate inverts: the held, cheaper category passes the 0.6 cash test that the preferred, dearer one just failed, so the money the hold was meant to accumulate is spent on exactly the queue being held.

The kill radius is posture-dependent and the design defends it in the wrong direction. ep.r = max(12, deepest ground weapon + 4) tiles. The file's own numbers: tank gun 8.0, SPG 20.4, MLRS 23.2. An armour wave gets 12 tiles, a tube-carrying wave 24-27 — four to five times the area. Every proximity-credited kill and razing, including the ones the design admits it cannot attribute ("something killed beside our push by an ally, or by the human, is credited to us"), accrues with area. fog_argument says that bound "is identical for all three postures so it cannot bias the ranking between them"; the code deliberately makes it not identical, so the residual the design waves off is the one term that differs between the arms.

And the attribution major is re-run, not fixed. `if (learnOn() && armNow) for (const u of army) if (!u._arm) u._arm = armNow;` backfills the entire army that existed before the loop turned on — bought under plain doctrine, at tech 1-2 — onto whichever posture happens to be argmax of the prior on the first think past the gate. Those hulls survive many pushes (launchGroundWave re-forms attackWave from army.slice), so the prior's favourite keeps the dominant cost share, and MIN_CRED then caps a newly explored posture at ~34% of the credit for the one push it actually shaped.

Smaller but real: the re-applied monoculture floor is computed as 35% of a total the posture has just inflated, so it hands back most of what gunline cut — worked on a tech-3, foot-heavy, line-heavy picture at grip 0.8, gunline's mbt share goes 19.8% (neutral) -> 11.9% (intended) -> 16.9% (after the floor), i.e. the floor absorbs about two thirds of the lean. `if (ep) learnSettle();` sits above the launch, but launchGroundWave's `const t = groundTarget(); if (!t) { waveT = 12; return; }` and the `else if (amphib.state === "idle")` fall-through both settle an episode when no push is committed, and no new episode opens (startAmphib never calls bookWave; only the landing at ai.js:4492 does). learnRazed fires on every gone=false -> gone=true transition and noteSighting sets `rec.gone = false` on re-sighting, so a falsely struck-off structure can be credited more than once. Measurement 8's "Sum(n) grows by exactly 1.0 per scored push" fails on the first scored push, which is inside the `if (!baseN)` branch that updates no arm. And "no new G.rng() call anywhere, so seeded replays stay deterministic" does not give what measurements 3 and 4 need: buildToward consumes G.rng() per candidate role whenever D.read < 1 (jit = 0.10*(1-read)), and the split gate changes how many buildToward calls happen per think, so the paired-seed learner/control comparison diverges from the first think and is not paired.

Verdict: the four named fatals are genuinely gone, but the redesign introduces a new structural one that reproduces their outcome, and its own headline mechanism (the split gate) is disabled by its release condition. BROKEN, and the corrections below are what would make it salvageable.

fatals.which: learnSettle() — the on-policy baseline cancels the learned signal
fatals.problem: `base` is a running mean of r over the pushes the POLICY took, and the policy is designed to commit. Once one posture is being pulled every push, base -> that posture's own mean, so A = r - base collapses to noise and q_incumbent decays to 0; the unpulled arms are still at their seeded q = 0. All three learned values are ~0 and score(a) = (1-lam)*p + bonus, i.e. the doctrine prior decides for the rest of the match. base's step is 1/min(baseN,6), so it catches up by push 3-4 — out of 6-8 settled pushes at Veteran, one of which is already spent setting the yardstick. The degeneracy_argument's Step 1 (base -> c + SUM f_a*mu(a)) is exactly this: with f concentrated, mu_bar -> mu_incumbent and every advantage goes to zero. The worked spread q = +0.12/-0.03/-0.13/-0.28 assumes f = (0.5,0.2,0.2,0.1) over 20 waves, which the policy's own commitment property contradicts. Same observable outcome as old fatal 1 — argmax returns one fixed arm for the whole battle — reached by a self-cancelling yardstick instead of a value clamp.
fatals.correction: Make the baseline estimate the COMMON term c, not E[r] under the behaviour policy. Fold the chosen arm's current estimate out before updating: keep `const A = r - base;` but write `base += (r - bChosen.q - base) / Math.min(++baseN, BASE_N);` using the PRE-update q of the arm that took the largest credit share. Then base -> c + mu_bar independently of the pull frequency and A stays unbiased however hard the policy commits. Add a forced opening round-robin so f is not degenerate: for the first min(3, nReady) settles, chooseArm() picks the fieldable posture with the smallest n (ties to the higher prior) instead of the argmax. Both are cheap over a 6-14 push horizon and are the only way three arms get a sample each.

fatals.which: armPrior()/chooseArm() — the prior gap is 0.60, not 0.30, so the manual cannot be overturned inside a match
fatals.problem: p = U.clamp((raw-m)*0.6, -0.30, 0.30). The maximum GAP between two priors is therefore 0.60 (both clamps saturated), not the 0.30 the design states — e.g. dm.heavy.mbt/heavy = 1.80 and the swarm roles at 0.55 gives p = (+0.30, -0.07, -0.30). The claim 'at lam=0.75 an observed advantage gap of 0.10 in exchange ratio overturns it' is off by 2x (it needs 0.20), and lam = 0.75*n/(n+2) only reaches 0.75 as n->inf: at n=4, lam=0.5 and the required learned gap is the full 0.60; at n=2 it is 1.00. Worked with p=(+0.30,-0.15,-0.15) and a catastrophic A = -0.5 every push, the incumbent is still argmax at pushes 1,2,3,4 and is first displaced at push 5 (score 0.0294 vs 0.0214 at push 3, -0.0131 vs 0.0259 at push 5) — past the end of a Veteran match. Combined with fatal 1 it is never displaced. This is the owner's 'don't let AI use the pre-trained knowledge entirely… with some flexibility' failing in the direction the design claims to have fixed.
fatals.correction: Either clamp the prior to +/-0.15 so the maximum gap really is 0.30 and the stated 0.10 arithmetic becomes true, or drop N0 from 2 to 1 (lam = 0.75*n/(n+1): 0.375 at the first pull, 0.60 at n=3) so the learned term reaches usable weight inside 6-14 pushes. Restate the worked example against the saturated gap of 0.60 rather than 0.30, and re-derive the 'overturns it' number from the tier's realistic n (2-6), not from the limit.

fatals.which: learnCommit() — ep.r is posture-dependent, so each arm is scored on a different ruler
fatals.problem: `ep.r = Math.max(12, reach + 4) * CFG.TILE` with reach = the wave's deepest ground weapon. The file's own figures (counterMix's line-break comment): tank gun 8.0 tiles, SPG 20.4, MLRS 23.2. An armour wave therefore gets a 12-tile credit disc (452 tiles^2) and a tube-carrying wave 24.4-27.2 tiles (1870-2324 tiles^2) — 4.1x to 5.1x the area. Both `kills` and `razed` are credited by proximity only, and fog_argument concedes the credit cannot distinguish who fired ('something killed beside our push by an ally, or by the human, is credited to us') while asserting that bound 'is identical for all three postures so it cannot bias the ranking between them.' The code makes it deliberately NOT identical, so the one un-attributable term in the reward scales with the very thing being compared, and it self-reinforces: gunline wins -> more tubes -> larger disc -> more free credit. The design fixed a rigged-short ruler by rigging it long.
fatals.correction: Make the ruler posture-independent. Compute it once per match from the union of what any fieldable posture could bring — `RULER = max over ARMS of (deepest in-era ground weapon reach for that posture's need-roles) + 4` — cache it beside `bookEra`, and use that single radius for every episode; or drop reach entirely and credit inside (wave spatial extent + a fixed 6-tile margin), which is posture-independent by construction. Then measurement 5's 'share of credited kills killed by somebody else' is a bound that cancels between arms, as the fog argument claims.

fatals.which: think() wave block — the retroactive u._arm backfill hands the pre-loop army to the prior's favourite
fatals.problem: `if (learnOn() && armNow) for (const u of army) if (!u._arm) u._arm = armNow;` runs over groundArmy() every think with no marker for 'was this unit already standing when the loop turned on'. armNow first becomes non-null when armReady() reaches two postures (tech 2, ~minute 5 at Elite), and on that very think the ENTIRE existing army — bought under plain doctrine, shaped by no posture — is permanently stamped with argmax of the prior. launchGroundWave re-forms attackWave from `army.slice(0, D.waveSize + 6)`, so those hulls recur in push after push and `ep.share` keeps handing the prior's favourite the dominant cost share. A posture tried later is then capped by MIN_CRED at ~34% of the credit for the one push it actually shaped, while the incumbent banks the rest of a result it did not cause. This is the attribution major the design says it made 'vanish structurally', re-run through the stamp instead of through the settle timing.
fatals.correction: Do not backfill. Stamp membership and posture separately: `if (!u._seenArmy) { u._seenArmy = 1; if (learnOn() && armNow) u._arm = armNow; }` — run the marker loop unconditionally (at every difficulty) so units that predate the loop are marked seen but left untagged. Then in learnCommit drop the `|| ep.arm` fallback and accumulate untagged cost into an `ep.legacy` bucket that is excluded from `w` and from the renormalisation, so a push made of pre-loop hulls teaches nobody rather than teaching the wrong posture.

fatals.which: think() wave block — the split gate's `!bought` release disables the one lever that changes the army's shape
fatals.problem: The release is `if (!bought) { ...build the held queue... }`, and buildToward returns false in the two most common states, neither of which is the structural unavailability the comment describes. (a) Saturation: when `queueLen(preferred) >= 2` the preferred call never runs, `bought` stays false, and the held queue is built anyway — the hold is released precisely while the preferred queue is working. (b) Scarcity: buildToward's `if (P.cash < P.factionCost(def) * 0.6) return false;` fires on the dearer category, the release then runs the cheaper held category, which passes the same 0.6 test — so the money the hold existed to accumulate is spent on the queue being held. The gate inverts under exactly the condition that makes it matter. Measurement 2(a) predicts a sustained 14/19/24-point infantry-share swing (the real deadband targets are 0.46/0.628 at Veteran, 0.43/0.654 at Elite, 0.40/0.68 at Commander = 17/22/28 points) and measurement 6 attributes a frequent release to 'the deadband is too narrow' — it will read as a narrow deadband while the real cause is the release predicate.
fatals.correction: Release only on structural impossibility, never on busy or broke. Have buildToward return a tri-state (e.g. return the string 'none' from its `if (sum <= 0) return false;` path and from the loop-exhausted path where every candidate hit `roleCool`/`lockReason`, keeping true/false for bought/broke), and gate the release on that: `if (hold !== -1 && preferredResult === 'none') { ...build the held queue... }`. Explicitly do NOT release when `queueLen(preferred) >= 2` — that is the gate working. Then add to measurement 6 a breakdown of the release cause (saturated / broke / no legal role); only the third should ever fire.

fatals.which: think() launch block + launchGroundWave()/startAmphib() — learnSettle() fires when no push is committed
fatals.problem: `if (ep) learnSettle();` sits above the launch, but the launch can fail after it. launchGroundWave begins `const t = groundTarget(); if (!t) { waveT = 12; return; }` — the episode has been scored and closed, attackWave still holds the previous wave (it is only reassigned after the target check), and no new episode opens; that wave then fights out its remaining kills, razings and casualties with ep === null and none of it is recorded. Separately, on a sea-split theatre `else if (amphib.state === "idle")` means that when a landing is already in progress neither branch runs and waveT is never reset, so the block re-enters every think with the settle already fired; startAmphib itself never calls bookWave (only the landing at ai.js:4492 does), so the gap between commit and landing is unscored while stanceMix is still leaning every purchase. Also in learnRazed's hook: noteSighting sets `rec.gone = false` on re-sighting, so a structure falsely struck off (forgetStale tests staleness at r.tx/r.ty, the origin tile, while noteContact tests pixel distance to e.x/e.y — a large building can be overlooked-but-unsighted at a sensor's edge) can transition gone=true more than once and be credited more than once.
fatals.correction: Move the settle to where a push is actually committed: delete `if (ep) learnSettle();` from the think block and call it at the top of learnCommit() instead — `if (ep) learnSettle();` immediately before `if (!ep) { epN++; ep = {...} }` — so the previous episode closes exactly when bookWave() commits the next one, on the ground launch and on the landing alike, and never on a launch that did not happen. Make the razing credit idempotent by keying it to the structure rather than the transition: `if (!r._razed) { r._razed = 1; learnRazed(r); }`, and clear `r._razed` in noteSighting's re-sight branch only if you also want a genuinely rebuilt structure to count again. Finally, fix measurement 8's own assertion — Sum(n) grows by 1.0 per scored push EXCEPT the first, which is inside the `if (!baseN)` branch and updates no arm — and drop the claim that seeded replays stay deterministic for measurements 3 and 4: buildToward consumes G.rng() per candidate role whenever D.read < 1 (jit = 0.10*(1-read)), and the split gate changes how many buildToward calls happen per think, so the paired-seed comparison diverges from the first think and is not paired.
